# roadkeep-gui

> A free desktop app for Windows and Linux that reads the backlogs roadkeep governs in every
> repository you point it at, one row per project, and hands a single line to Claude Code
> with the `brief` roadkeep printed for it. It never writes a governed file: every change is
> a `roadkeep` command the app composes as an argument list, shows, and leaves the engine to
> run. Built with Electron and React, in a sandboxed renderer. MIT, in `LICENSE`.

There is an installer to download, from
[the release page](https://github.com/alegauss/roadkeep-gui/releases/latest): a per-user
Windows installer and a Linux AppImage, both unsigned for now. No macOS build has been made.
Neither carries roadkeep: each project answers through its own committed launcher or the
`roadkeep` on PATH (`pip install roadkeep`). Claude Code is needed only to hand a line over.

roadkeep itself is at [alegauss.github.io/roadkeep](https://alegauss.github.io/roadkeep/).
This app is an unofficial companion by the same author, not affiliated with Anthropic.

## For agents

Every route of this site has a Markdown twin beside it, the same page converted from the
same render with the navigation, the footer and the calls to action dropped. Read
`<route>/index.md` instead of the HTML: the landing page is
[`/index.md`](https://alegauss.github.io/roadkeep-gui/index.md). The routes, their twins and
their byte sizes are in
[`manifest.json`](https://alegauss.github.io/roadkeep-gui/manifest.json).

Every count those pages state (the verbs, the languages, the non-goals, the scan depth) is
generated at build time from this repository's source, so the twin is the place to read a
number rather than this file.

## What it does

- **The portfolio**: one row per governed project under the folders you named, with its open
  and startable lines, the next ready line, the last gate verdict and which roadkeep answered.
  Nothing is summed across projects.
- **Discovery**: no default root. You name folders and a depth; the scan looks for
  `roadkeep.toml`, skips hidden and build directories, and groups worktrees by reading git's
  files without running git.
- **One project**: its lines filtered by `list` arguments, a tab per governed file, the gate
  with the fix command roadkeep offers per finding, and a task screen joined by `brief`.
- **Filing a line**: a form measured against roadkeep's `budget`, the block's existing lines
  beside it, and the exact `roadkeep add` command shown before it runs.
- **Hand to Claude Code**: `brief --claim`, then your own `claude` in the project root with the
  brief verbatim; the window carries the stream, the permission questions, the edited files
  and what moved according to the files. It sets no model, no permission mode and writes no
  `.claude` settings.
- **Explain / How to check it**: read-only one-shot questions to Claude Code, limited to read
  tools, with nothing kept in session history.
- **Live refresh**: the governed files are watched, and one `ship` arrives as one refresh.

## What it refuses

The non-goals live in
[`docs/ROADMAP.md`](https://github.com/alegauss/roadkeep-gui/blob/main/docs/ROADMAP.md) and
are rendered on the landing page from there. In short: no Markdown parsed by the app, no
write to a governed file, no rule compiled in, no engine it cannot name, no field it
composes, no dates or burndown, no git, no account, no issue tracker.
